title: EngineRunManifest
description: One (engine, model) cell's execution record for the engine-performance layer (docs/engine-performance-plan.md). Every accuracy or latency result row must carry one of these so a delta can be attributed to engine/quantization/sampling/hardware rather than left ambiguous. Accuracy and latency passes for the same cell are two separate manifests (separate runs), never one.

run_id.description: Unique per execution, e.g. ULID. Distinct from case id.

pass_type.description: Which pass produced this manifest. An accuracy sweep and a latency pass over the same cell are never the same run (eval_bench/repetition.py's n=5 shuffle sweep is itself a load generator and would corrupt its own timing numbers). accuracy_under_load is the concurrency-vs-correctness probe (docs/engine-performance-plan.md 'なぜこの層を足すのか' > 並行負荷下でのツールコーリング精度維持) -- kept as its own pass_type rather than reusing 'accuracy' with cell.concurrency set, so its concurrency=1 control point and high-concurrency point are never silently pooled with the plain accuracy sweep's implicit concurrency=1 baseline.

engine.description: transformers_hf is the naive baseline (no serving-level batching). ollama is optional/deprioritized: it wraps llama_cpp's inference core, so engine deltas against llama_cpp may be near-null and must be reported as such, not hidden.

tool_catalog_version.description: The top-level 'version' of whichever catalog file backed this run. Determined by tool_stage, not by pass_type: tool_stage=10 must reference schema/tools.json's version (the original 40-tool catalog, identical to Article 1's), tool_stage=50/100 must reference schema/tools_extended.json's version (the 100-tool catalog: the same 40 plus 60 added for this layer, generated by scripts/generate_extended_catalog.py). Never compare results across different catalog versions at the same nominal stage -- the tool sets, and therefore selection difficulty, differ.

model.description: 8B-class model id/name, pinned to a specific checkpoint (see docs/engine-performance-plan.md's model-size decision).

quantization.description: e.g. 'gguf-q4_k_m', 'awq-4bit', 'fp16-none'. Must be held equivalent across engines being compared in the same cell pair; if an engine can't match, exclude that cell rather than silently adjusting.

sampling_params.description: Every knob the adapters send is recorded. top_k/min_p are required because engine defaults for them differ (llama.cpp server top_k=40/min_p=0.05 vs the model generation_config's top_k=20/min_p=0), so an unrecorded value cannot be assumed equal across engines.

tool_stage.description: Shared by both accuracy and latency pass_type: [10, 50, 100] (see docs/engine-performance-plan.md). Stage 10 uses ONLY the original 40-tool catalog (schema/tools.json) -- same tools dict Article 1 uses, so results overlay Article 1's own stage=10 numbers exactly. Stages 50/100 use the extended 100-tool catalog (schema/tools_extended.json: original 40 + 60 added for this layer, same ERP domain, same module structure -- deepened existing modules and/or plausible additional ERP modules, e.g. production/project management; not confusability-engineered like the original 40, but must be genuinely plausible business tools, not generic placeholders, per external precedent (tau-bench, BFCL, ToolBench all scale within a coherent domain rather than mixing unrelated ones) -- obviously-synthetic filler risks teaching the model an 'ignore oddly-named tools' shortcut that would distort the very large-catalog effect this stage is meant to measure). Passing the extended dict for a stage=10 run would change the padding candidate pool and break the Article-1-overlay property -- must not be done.

prompt_layout.description: Ordering of the stable prefix (system prompt + tool schema + few-shot) versus the variable query within the prompt. stable_first (query last) maximizes prefix-cache hit rate under each engine's default-on caching (vLLM V1 and llama.cpp server's cache_prompt are both enabled by default -- an ON/OFF toggle was rejected as unrealistic, see docs/engine-performance-plan.md). query_first breaks the cache for everything after the query since prefix caching matches from the start of the sequence. Unlike a pure cache toggle, this CAN affect correctness (position bias / lost-in-the-middle). 2026-09-10: the harness switched from raw completion endpoints to each engine's chat/tools API (see docs/engine-performance-plan.md's '比較可能性の規律' section) -- chat templates render system(tools)-then-user(query) by structural contract, so query_first can no longer be produced and is out of scope. The enum keeps both values for record-keeping/forward-compatibility, but every manifest this project writes will have prompt_layout=stable_first.

concurrency.description: Number of requests fired concurrently. 1 = serialized (the attribution-safe default). >1 is only meaningful for engines with request-level batching (vllm; llama_cpp's --parallel slots are a fixed-reservation approximation; transformers_hf has no request scheduler or shared KV at all and is excluded from the concurrency axis entirely, reported at concurrency=1 only as the no-serving-optimization control point -- see docs/engine-performance-plan.md). Required for pass_type latency and accuracy_under_load; must be absent for plain pass_type accuracy, which is concurrency=1 by convention and never states it explicitly (see the allOf rule forbidding it below).

instance_type.description: e.g. 'g6.xlarge'. Fixed across all cells in this plan so hardware is never a confound -- see docs/engine-performance-plan.md.

repetition.description: Required when pass_type == accuracy; mirrors eval_bench.repetition.aggregate_repeated's shape.

results.description: Shape depends on pass_type; see the allOf below.

allOf.$comment: Plain accuracy manifests are concurrency=1 by convention (docs/engine-performance-plan.md: 'accuracy pass is concurrency=1 for all engines'). Forbid stating cell.concurrency at all here so a concurrency-under-load data point can never be mistaken for -- or silently pooled with -- the plain sweep's baseline; that probe is pass_type accuracy_under_load instead.

results.description: eval_bench.latency.summarize output (docs/adr/0003-latency-pass-verdict.md). Percentiles are over the measured requests that completed; timeouts are counted in n_timeouts and as exceedances in slo, never in the percentiles.

warmup_excluded.description: Warmup requests must always be excluded from reported percentiles.

n_requests.description: Measured requests, fixed before the run (>= 299 for a main run).

tpot_ms.description: (total - TTFT) / (output tokens - 1). Null only if no request produced 2+ tokens.

tokens_per_sec.description: Per request: output tokens / total latency.

warmup.description: Perf Analyzer's stability rule in count_windows form: one window = one cycle of the case set.

prefix_cache.description: Absent for transformers_hf (no prefix cache). The cache is on, as in production, and reset at the cell boundary (docs/adr/0003).

reference_accuracy.description: The measured requests' tool calls scored like the accuracy pass, as a reference only (docs/adr/0003 J): sampled at the cell's temperature with a request id appended to each query, so never used for a verdict.

allOf.$comment: The concurrency-vs-correctness probe (the third pass, docs/adr/0002). Run on every configuration that holds concurrency 16 by the capacity check (docs/adr/0005), not on a named engine (ADR-0002 addendum 2026-10-19); transformers_hf has no concurrent serving. Both the concurrency=1 control point and the high-concurrency point use this pass_type, distinguished only by cell.concurrency -- never pooled with plain accuracy's implicit concurrency=1 baseline.

accuracy_results_base.description: Shared by pass_type accuracy and accuracy_under_load -- both are eval_bench.repetition.aggregate_repeated output, differing only in which cell fields are legal (see the allOf branches above) and in whether capacity_check is a defined property.

arg_exact_mean.description: Null iff no case in this stage/model had exact-scored fields to evaluate. Computed by eval_bench.repetition.aggregate_repeated, pooled over only the trials where the metric was applicable (selection succeeded on a positive case with scoreable fields of this kind).

slo_verdict.description: One latency class (MLPerf's Llama 3.1 8B limits). A request exceeds if it timed out or its TTFT or TPOT is over the limit; the exceedance rate is judged against 1% with one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson bounds.

capacity_check.description: Whether the KV cache held every request at once (docs/adr/0005). Required by the harness (eval_bench/runner.py) for every concurrency>1 cell of a served engine; the schema cannot compare its own fields, so required.tokens <= capacity.tokens is enforced there. A cell failing the pre-check never runs (recorded unsupported); a failed post-check is written with post_check.ok=false and its numbers are not used for a verdict.

capacity.description: vLLM: /metrics vllm:cache_config_info (num_gpu_blocks x block_size). llama.cpp: the --ctx-size the server was started with (--kv-unified: one cache shared by every slot; llama-server reports no total), plus /props n_ctx as per_slot_tokens.

per_slot_tokens.description: llama.cpp: /props n_ctx, the per-slot limit; capped at the model's training context (Qwen3-8B: 40,960) when --ctx-size exceeds it. The longest request must fit in it.

tokens.description: concurrency x (per_request_tokens + margin) rounded up to whole units.

restarts.description: vLLM only: restarts after a startup came out short of the requirement.

startup_log_max_concurrency.description: vLLM startup log's 'Maximum concurrency', for cross-checking only.

preemptions.description: vLLM: vllm:num_preemptions delta over the cell.

queue_time.description: vLLM: vllm:request_queue_time_seconds deltas, recorded only (not a discard condition, docs/adr/0005 3).

length_finished.description: llama.cpp: responses that stopped at the length limit.
